newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Indians hold 40 hostage, demand services.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Indians hold 40 hostage, demand services.

text.p: Indians are holding 40 people hostage in northeastern Brazil, demanding better roads, health services and education facilities for their reserve, officials said on Monday.

A police spokesman in the town of Grajau in Maranhao state said Indians from the Guajajara tribe on Friday hijacked a bus and truck after blocking a road with logs and took the drivers and passengers to their village.

He said the Indians were demanding that the only road running through their reserve, recently washed away by heavy rains, be repaired. They also complained about a lack of health and education services.

An official of the Indian umbrella group Capoib said the Guajajaras had vowed to keep their hostages until Julio Gaiger, head of the National Indian Foundation (Funai), and Justice Minister Nelson Jobim showed up to negotiate.

A spokeswoman for Funai said its regional administrator in Maranhao had travelled to the area to try to secure the release of the hostages but that due to the reserve's remoteness he had not yet been able to phone back any information.

The 10,200 Guajajara Indians in Maranhao have established a reputation for not shirking conflict. Last month, they kidnapped three officials from the Maranhao state education ministry, demanding a teacher be sent to work in their reserve. The officials managed to escape.

In July last year, the Guajajara clashed with landless families settling on their territory and in 1992 they fought against the construction of a road and blocked a railway used by state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, demanding compensation.
